expectations.evidence: (blocking) No ownership check on the source account: `src/routes/transfers.js:23` ... never compares `owner_id` to `req.user.id`
(blocking) Amount and destination are not validated ... `amount: -5000` ... `amount` is `"100"` or `1.5` ... reject `fromId === toId`
(blocking) Balance check and the two UPDATEs run outside a transaction ... Both read the balance as 100, both pass the check, and the balance ends at -$100.
(blocking) The state-changing route has no CSRF protection ... `session.js` documents the cookie as `sameSite=none`

(blocking) An unhandled async error can crash the process ... `fromId` is unknown or missing. `from.rows[0].balance_cents` throws a TypeError; also: `toId` doesn't exist: the credit UPDATE matches 0 rows
(should_fix) The audit-log write is fire-and-forget ... isn't awaited and runs outside the transfer
(should_fix) replace `proc(r, u, d, flag)` with a clearly named function ... `flag` is always `true`, so the `{ ok: true }` branch is dead code
(should_fix) The new route has no tests: `test/`
(should_fix) `lodash` was added, but nothing requires it. express was bumped from `^4.19.2` to `^4.21.1`.
(should_fix) `format.js` was reformatted to 4-space indents, single quotes and no semicolons, with no behaviour change.
(should_fix) The PR title, description and commits don't meet the repo's rules

expectations.text: Rates every answer-key blocker as blocking

A cross-site form post with an empty body reaches the handler and triggers the crash, so missing CSRF is exploitable for DoS today

grader.notes: Found every seeded issue. Each finding has a concrete 'Breaks when' scenario, a location and a fix, and the severities closely match the key. Its CSRF analysis is precise but says transfers can't happen cross-site today; the review still keeps CSRF as a blocker.
